question.problem: Ann and Steven are playing a card game. Ann chooses a card at random from a deck of cards labeled $15$ through $40.$ If the number she picks is greater or equal to $20$ and less than $25,$ Ann wins, otherwise Steven wins. What is the probability that Ann wins the game?
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the card number Ann picks. From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U\{15,16,…,40\},$ and we wish to compute $P(20\le X<25).$

In general, if $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{|S|}, & x\in S \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $X∼U\{15,16,…,40\},$ and the set $S=\{15,16,…,40\}$ has $|S|=40-15+1=26$ items. So, we have

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{26}, & x=15,16,…,40 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

In $S,$ the items that satisfy $20\le X<25$ are $20,21,22,23,24.$ There are $5$ of these elements. Therefore,

$$
P(20\le X<25)=5\cdot \frac{1}{26}=\frac{5}{26}.
$$
